question.worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y) \\  & =2xy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy) \\  & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${f}_{xyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{xy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
